name: law_firm_software_014_custodian_collection_gap_audit
instruction: Run the custodian collection-gap audit, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. The firm's hold-acknowledgement policy (HOLD-ACK-01 in firm_policies) governs which holds are in scope: active holds that have been in effect for at least the episode row's gap_grace_days days. Every custodian named on an in-scope hold is supposed to have data collected for that hold's matter -- a custodian counts as covered only by a collection belonging to the hold's own matter; a collection filed under a different matter does not cover the custodian. For every in-scope hold custodian with no covering collection, push one ops_reports row (report='collection_gap', batch_code) identifying the hold, the custodian, the matter, and how long the hold has been in effect (whole days from issue to the episode date). Then push one summary row (report='collection_gap_summary', batch_code) with the total number of gaps. Finally age the gaps this batch reported into the firm's standard hold-aging buckets (under_30 / 30_90 / over_90 by days since the hold was issued) and push one ops_reports row per non-empty bucket (report='collection_gap_aging', batch_code) derived from the SAME gap rows this batch produced. No other ops_reports rows for this batch under those three report names may exist. Do not modify ediscovery_holds or ediscovery_collections. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: Custodians of active holds whose data was never collected (planted: 20 bulk holds with no matching collection by construction plus the 4 hand-authored uncollected custodians on HOLD-2026-001/002/003; the live in-scope gap set recomputes per episode from the seed snapshot -- snapshot-confirmed 12 gap pairs at the minimum grace window in the current snapshot). A naive audit that skips the grace window or counts released/suspended holds over- or under-reports.

5 cross-matter collections (COL-2026-XMAT-0..4, snapshot-confirmed: 5) cover their custodian under a DIFFERENT matter than the custodian's own hold -- a collection under a different matter does not cover the custodian. Naive any-collection matching misses exactly these gaps whenever the custodian's own hold is in scope; the per-matter rule (HOLD-ACK-01's coverage definition) counts them.

the grace window is an episode knob (gap_grace_days 15-45): the in-scope hold set and the gap set move every episode, so memorized gap lists go stale (snapshot-confirmed: the window boundary splits holds at every episode date).

success_criteria.summary: One collection_gap row per (in-scope active hold, uncovered custodian) pair -- coverage means a collection under the HOLD's own matter referencing that custodian's contact_id; cross-matter collections do not cover. One collection_gap_summary row with the matching total, and one collection_gap_aging row per non-empty bucket derived from the same gap rows. Every derived aggregate is confirmed two independent ways (raw-row filter and SQL) which must agree with each other and with the written rows. ediscovery_holds and ediscovery_collections are canary-checked byte-identical.

checks.expect: one collection_gap row per real gap plus one summary row and one aging row per non-empty bucket, exact
the gap set agrees between the Python per-matter coverage filter and a SQL coverage aggregate
matching a custodian's collection under a DIFFERENT matter as coverage produces a wrong gap set and FAILs; acting on released/suspended holds FAILs
